c.tagline: Belgium's canal-laced university city of medieval towers, vegetarian cuisine, and student energy.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered with regulated rates; most rides are booked by phone, app, or picked up at a taxi stand rather than hailed on the street.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; 101 is the direct Belgian police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the Korenmarkt, Patershol and festival crowds, especially during the Gentse Feesten; watch bikes and bags near Gent-Sint-Pieters station at night.

hood_desc: A maze of narrow medieval streets just north of Gravensteen castle, packed with some of Ghent's best restaurants and bars in restored gabled houses; ideal for food lovers who want to be steps from the main sights.
The pedestrianized heart of Ghent around the Belfry, Saint Bavo's Cathedral, and the Graslei/Korenlei waterfront; the natural base for first-timers who want everything walkable.
The lively student strip near Ghent University's main campus, lined with bars and late-night venues; suits younger travelers who want an energetic, budget-friendly nightlife scene.
A historic market square once the site of public gatherings and executions, now ringed by cafes, breweries, and independent shops; good for travelers who enjoy markets and craft-beer culture.
A quieter, redeveloped waterfront district along the old docks, with a marina, parks, and new housing; suits travelers seeking a calmer, residential feel away from the tourist core.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality throughout Belgium.

transit.hours: Trams and buses generally run from about 5:00 AM to midnight, with a limited weekend night-bus network filling the gap.
transit.pay: Pay with a rechargeable De Lijn card, the De Lijn app, or contactless bank card tap-in on trams and buses; single paper tickets bought on board cost more.
transit.note: Ghent's compact center is best explored on foot or by bike; De Lijn trams and buses cover the wider city, and Gent-Sint-Pieters station links to Brussels and beyond by rail.

transit.m: Direct train to Gent-Sint-Pieters (~50 min, hourly)

tip.r: Service is included by law in restaurant and cafe bills; rounding up or leaving about 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.
